title: Q18 — does the lexicographic org tiebreak decide anything, on real data? (W-22 / I-7)
status: PREPARED — requested through the governed trusted-host path. This lane holds no deployed credential and does not attempt one.
$comment: A DEDICATED artifact, deliberately not an amendment to q15-authority-census.json. Promoting amended SQL into that file inherits its stored hash and fails query_hash_mismatch — a trap this program has already paid for once. Q15 is consumed and is not retried.
why_this_question: W-22 removes a silent authority decision: `chooseOrgAndRoleKeysFromMembershipRows` collapses a multi-org principal to one org by sorting UUIDs (`admin`/`ops` rows win, else the lexicographically smallest `org_id`). The plan's exit is `no authority decision depends on UUID ordering`. What the plan cannot say is what removing it COSTS, because that depends on whether any principal is actually multi-org. This is the same shape as `Q15-A1` for W-20: if the population is zero the workstream collapses from an architectural change to a deletion plus a lock; if it is non-zero, removing the tiebreak is lockout-class and must be sequenced behind an explicit request org.
read_only_basis: One SELECT. No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ALTER/CREATE/DROP/GRANT, no DO block, no writing function. Validated with `validateReadOnlySql` and executed against a local PostgreSQL to prove it parses and returns — those cert-tenant rows are NOT the census and are recorded nowhere.

data_minimization.returns: counts, and role keys already public in the catalog
data_minimization.never_returns: user ids, names, emails, phone numbers, org names, child or family data
data_minimization.identifier_policy: No query selects a user_id or an org_id. Every answer is an aggregate; a principal is counted, never identified. If a specific principal must be examined, that is a follow-up question with its own approval, not a widening of this one.

questions.question: How many principals hold memberships in more than one organization?
questions.decides: Zero means the tiebreak never fires on real data and W-22 becomes a deletion plus RL-lock, exactly as Q15-A1 collapsed W-20. Non-zero is the population a removal would affect.

questions.question: Of the multi-org principals, how many hold admin/ops rows in more than one organization — the pool the tiebreak actually sorts?
questions.decides: The code sorts admin/ops rows when any exist, and all rows otherwise. A principal multi-org in custom roles only is sorted by the second branch; one multi-org in admin/ops is sorted by the first. The two have different blast radii and this separates them.

questions.question: Distribution: how many principals hold memberships in exactly N organizations?
questions.note: A tail of one principal in nine orgs is a different remediation from ninety principals in two.

questions.question: For multi-org principals, does the chosen org differ from the org holding their strongest role — i.e. is the sort discarding authority rather than merely choosing between equals?
questions.decides: Non-zero means the tiebreak is not a presentation default but an authority narrowing that is already happening today.

decision_rules.W-22_is_a_deletion_iff: Q18-A1 returns zero principals. The sort is then unreachable and removing it cannot change any principal's resolved org.
decision_rules.W-22_is_lockout_class_iff: Q18-A1 is non-zero. Removal must then be sequenced behind an explicit request org, and the affected population is Q18-A1.
decision_rules.the_tiebreak_is_already_narrowing_iff: Q18-C1 is non-zero — in which case W-22 is not only removing a silent decision, it is restoring authority the sort is discarding today.

combined_query:
WITH memberships AS (
  SELECT ur.user_id,
         ur.org_id,
         lower(btrim(ur.role::text)) AS role_key
  FROM public.user_roles ur
  WHERE NULLIF(lower(btrim(ur.role::text)), '') IS NOT NULL
),
per_principal AS (
  SELECT m.user_id,
         count(DISTINCT m.org_id) AS orgs,
         count(DISTINCT m.org_id) FILTER (WHERE m.role_key IN ('admin', 'ops')) AS portal_orgs
  FROM memberships m
  GROUP BY m.user_id
),
a1 AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS multi_org_principals,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM per_principal) AS principals_total
  FROM per_principal p
  WHERE p.orgs > 1
),
a2 AS (
  SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.portal_orgs > 1) AS multi_org_in_portal_roles,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.orgs > 1 AND p.portal_orgs <= 1) AS multi_org_custom_only
  FROM per_principal p
  WHERE p.orgs > 1
),
b1 AS (
  SELECT p.orgs AS organizations, count(*) AS principals
  FROM per_principal p
  GROUP BY p.orgs
),
chosen AS (
  SELECT p.user_id,
         (SELECT min(m.org_id::text)
            FROM memberships m
           WHERE m.user_id = p.user_id
             AND (p.portal_orgs = 0 OR m.role_key IN ('admin', 'ops'))) AS chosen_org
  FROM per_principal p
  WHERE p.orgs > 1
),
c1 AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS multi_org_principals_examined,
         count(*) FILTER (
           WHERE EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM memberships m
             WHERE m.user_id = ch.user_id
               AND m.org_id::text <> ch.chosen_org
               AND m.role_key IN ('admin', 'ops')
           )
         ) AS discards_a_portal_role_elsewhere
  FROM chosen ch
),
answered AS (
  SELECT 'Q18-A1' AS question_id, (SELECT count(*) FROM a1) AS row_count
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q18-A2', (SELECT count(*) FROM a2)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q18-B1', (SELECT count(*) FROM b1)
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q18-C1', (SELECT count(*) FROM c1)
)
SELECT question_id, kind, payload
FROM (
  SELECT ans.question_id, 'row_count' AS kind,
         jsonb_build_object('row_count', ans.row_count) AS payload
  FROM answered ans
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q18-A1', 'row', to_jsonb(a1) FROM a1
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q18-A2', 'row', to_jsonb(a2) FROM a2
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q18-B1', 'row', to_jsonb(b1) FROM b1
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Q18-C1', 'row', to_jsonb(c1) FROM c1
) census
ORDER BY question_id, kind, payload::text;
combined_query_shape: Rows are (question_id, kind, payload). Every question emits exactly one kind='row_count' row even when it matches nothing, so 'returned zero' stays distinguishable from 'never ran' — the decision rules turn on zero/non-zero and a silently skipped query would read as a pass.
combined_query_hash_absent_deliberately: No hash is stored. The validator compares a stored hash against what it is about to run and fails query_hash_mismatch on any drift; the executing channel should hash what it runs.
